title: Handshake, entropy and TLS authority
summary: WebSocket protocol code does not own TLS credentials or production entropy. dev3 optionally binds RFC 6455 SHA-1 accept calculation to the estate crypto.auth authority while keeping handshake nonce and frame-mask bytes behind an injected entropy interface.
invariants: WebSocketHandshakeCrypto remains the protocol-facing handshake authority contract.
WebSocketMaskSource remains the protocol-facing frame-mask authority contract.
WebSocketPlatformCrypto.cls is optional and separate from WebSocketAccess.cls.
WebSocketCryptoAuthHandshake uses crypto.auth/0.1 SHA-1 for Sec-WebSocket-Accept and standard base64 encoding.
WebSocketCryptoAuthMaskSource obtains four-byte masks from the same injected WebSocketEntropySource authority.
Production entropy is not bundled or claimed by dev3; the final estate randomness binding remains a qualification gate.
TLS certificate, trust and private-key material remain in Socket Provider / SocketSecurityMaterialProvider.
wss composition therefore uses the common TLS/socket authority; WebSocket does not acquire OpenSSL or TLS sockets directly.
The RFC 6455 example key/accept vector is a deterministic contract fixture, not a production randomness mechanism.
